definitions.explanation: A number in the hundreds — one that has three places (100–999). {桁|けた} counts digits or decimal places, so {三桁|さんけた} means three places.

examples.japanese: パスワードは{三桁|さんけた}の{数字|すうじ}だ。
examples.english: The password is a three-digit number.

examples.japanese: {売上|うりあげ}がついに{三桁|さんけた}に{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: Sales finally reached three digits (the hundreds).

examples.japanese: {二桁|ふたけた}の{掛|か}け{算|ざん}をすると{答|こた}えが{三桁|さんけた}になることがある。
examples.english: Multiplying two-digit numbers can give a three-digit answer.

notes:
{桁|けた} means a digit or decimal place, so {三桁|さんけた} is a number with three places — the hundreds, from 100 to 999. The pattern extends to other counts of digits.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三桁|さんけた}の{数字|すうじ}: a three-digit number
- {三桁|さんけた}に{乗|の}る: to reach three digits (the hundreds)

RELATED:
- {二桁|ふたけた}: two digits (10–99)
- {四桁|よんけた}: four digits (1,000–9,999)
